title: Swiss government websites are published in the official Swiss languages and English, and every language version is expected to carry equivalent information. In practice, translation errors and unsynchronised content updates introduce semantic differences between versions. SwissGov-RSD is a benchmark of 224 multi-parallel Swiss government documents in English, German, French and Italian, with human annotations of semantic differences for the EN–DE, EN–FR and EN–IT document pairs.

i.c: Swiss government websites are published in the official Swiss languages and English, and every language version is expected to carry equivalent information. In practice, translation errors and unsynchronised content updates introduce semantic differences between versions. SwissGov-RSD is a benchmark of 224 multi-parallel Swiss government documents in English, German, French and Italian, with human annotations of semantic differences for the EN–DE, EN–FR and EN–IT document pairs.

title: Given two related documents in different languages, predict for each token how strongly its meaning differs from the corresponding content in the other document. Systems should identify both symmetric differences and asymmetric ones such as additions and omissions.

i.c: Given two related documents in different languages, predict for each token how strongly its meaning differs from the corresponding content in the other document. Systems should identify both symmetric differences and asymmetric ones such as additions and omissions.

title: What exactly am I predicting?
b

For each token in a document, a score for how strongly its meaning differs from the corresponding content in the other-language document. Both symmetric differences and asymmetric ones (additions, omissions) are in scope.

i.c: For each token in a document, a score for how strongly its meaning differs from the corresponding content in the other-language document. Both symmetric differences and asymmetric ones (additions, omissions) are in scope.

title: Which language pairs are evaluated?
b
EN–DE, EN–FR and EN–IT. Scores are computed per pair and macro-averaged across the three.

i.c: EN–DE, EN–FR and EN–IT. Scores are computed per pair and macro-averaged across the three.

title: How is my submission scored?
b

Token-level Spearman correlation between your predicted scores and the gold scores, macro-averaged across the three pairs — higher is better. Efficiency and innovation/creativity are secondary criteria. Use the provided evaluation script; it defines the preprocessing and how punctuation is handled.

i.c: Token-level Spearman correlation between your predicted scores and the gold scores, macro-averaged across the three pairs — higher is better. title: Can I use the test set while building my solution?
b
No. The repos include all splits, but the test set must not enter development in any form — no training, no prompt examples, no tuning against it. Doing so disqualifies the result.

title: Do I have to fine-tune Apertus?
b

No. Fine-tuning and adapters are one option among several. Prompting strategies, chunking/decomposition, structured generation, self-consistency and post-processing are all encouraged — including combinations. A strong prompting-only solution is completely valid.

i.c: Do I have to fine-tune Apertus?

title: Which model should I use — 8B or 70B?
b

Either; both Apertus v1.5 sizes are in scope. The 8B is lighter to iterate on; the 70B may score higher but costs more compute. Since efficiency is a secondary criterion, a well-tuned 8B solution can be competitive.
